title: Dealing with rubbish without losing the day
target: How to keep on top of rubbish in Supermarket Simulator while treating it as the separate job it is.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with bins and bags available
Somewhere to put a bag out
A janitor if you have one

steps.do: Separate rubbish from dirt and dust before you start, because they are different jobs.
steps.because: cleaning is split into named actions for dirt, dust and rubbish, with a kind that tells them apart (CleanDirtAction, CleanDustAction, CleanGarbageAction, CleaningType)

steps.do: Expect rubbish to be produced rather than only left behind.
steps.because: the game keeps a generator and a manager for rubbish (GarbageGenerator, GarbageManager)

steps.do: Treat the mess as objects in the world, not as a texture on the floor.
steps.because: there is a rubbish object and a trash object of the game's own (Garbage, Trash)

steps.do: Use the bins and bags the game provides rather than your own arrangement.
steps.because: rubbish has bins and bags of its own (TrashBin, TrashBag)

steps.do: Count going to the rubbish as a step of its own when you plan a lap of the shop.
steps.because: going to the rubbish is a step of its own (GoToTrash)

steps.do: Know that putting a bag out is an action which can be switched off.
steps.because: the bag has its own interaction and the action can be disabled (TrashbagInteraction, DisableTrashBagAction)

steps.do: Look for the bin that comes with the thing you placed.
steps.because: the ice cream stand has a bin of its own (IceCreamTrashBin)

steps.do: Hand the job to a janitor if you have one, and it will keep its own states per kind of mess.
steps.because: the janitor runs through a manager and a state machine, with separate cleaning states for dirt, dust and rubbish, and it works in a shared shop (JanitorManager, Janitor, DirtCleaningState, DustCleaningState, GarbageCleaningState, NetworkJanitor)

commonMistakes: Mopping as if rubbish were dirt and then wondering why the mess is still there.
Filling bins you cannot reach instead of using the bags.
Forgetting that a bag left ready to go out is not the same as gone.
Buying a janitor and then doing the cleaning yourself anyway.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
